content.text: The document contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall, or volume-cap provision binding the Company.

input.quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month.
input.rationale: The only payment obligation on the Company (Section 3, para p0019) is a pure revenue share — 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 per-month threshold — so fees accrue solely from actual sales generated through the Site. The $11,000 figure is a floor below which nothing is owed (a benefit to us), not a minimum spend. HDI bears the design, development, hosting and promotion costs (paras p0006, p0014), and there is no take-or-pay, minimum purchase, shortfall make-whole, or cap/floor on Company volume anywhere in the text; searches for "minimum", "commit" and "fee" return no commitment language. The term is a single year with rolling one-year renewals terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (para p0024), which satisfies even the fallback exit requirement. Separately, Section 4.2(a) (para p0026) imposes a Termination Payment if the Company terminates, calculated as (trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000) / 2. That is an exit charge measured by actual achieved sales rather than a penalty for failing to hit a committed volume, so it does not create a take-or-pay obligation under this rule; it is priced-exit exposure properly addressed under the termination-fee/early-exit rule rather than redlined here. No edit is warranted for MINCOMMIT.
